QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_21

question.text: 'Most Favoured Nation' (MFN) provisions in side-letters of an AIF:

answer.text: Only apply to distributors, not investors.

Entitle an investor to elect the benefit of rights contained in OTHER investors' side-letters, and potentially also the right to view those side-letters; the Sponsor/Manager should regularise their use so that special or additional rights are not afforded arbitrarily.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 11.3.1: MFN entitles an investor to elect the benefit of rights in other investors' side-letters (and potentially view them). Sponsor/Manager must regularise MFN to ensure arbitrary preferential treatment doesn't arise — consistent with fiduciary duty and fair-dealing. The Trap: MFN is not illegal, just regulated/regularised. It applies to investors (not distributors). It is not a priority-redemption guarantee.
